Persis Regibus olim in usu fuisse tradit, ab Athenæo l.4.

l.i: Si vini copia adesset, quantum qisqe poscce-

main_text.l: ret; sin minùs, ex ego fingulis præberet. Plut. in Agesilai
apophth. Potum, inqit historicus sacer, præbebant (ministri
nimirum regii) scyphis aureis, qe subinde iterabant, vel muta-
bant; præbebant autem, ut vinum regni, i.e. regium, regiis
usibus destinatum; ita plurimum, copiosum idem, juxta regis
manum, i.e. pro regiâ facultate; prout tam amplis opi-
bus instructum regem convivis suis suppeditare par erat: in
eo maximè convivio, qo regni sui divitias splendorémque osten-
tare ambiebat. ut est versu 4. Sic omnino [illegible, ~6 letters] dici verè
poterat; cum qi ullâ in parte cohiberet, planè nullus esset;
sed unicuique pro libitu suo, qodcunque, qandocunque, quan-
tumcunque poscperet, à ministris qibusqe porrigeretur: qem
ego verborum istorum sensum, nec ambiguus id, avtumo ge-
nuinum.

page.notes: Greek passages in the first lines and the Greek words in the body (e.g. the Greek after "cum famulis", "Cumanus", "Denique", and "Potum") are only partly legible at this scan resolution and are marked illegible where I could not read them letter by letter. The left-margin notes are cropped fragments and mostly unreadable; I have marked them illegible rather than guess. The text "[illegible]" in the margin notes stands for such fragments. The Greek heading line at the top and the Hebrew-like abbreviation "ꝑ" near "dici" are doubtful.
